units.translation: to be dishonored with exile driven by the people.
τοῦ δήμου ἐλαθεὶ [driven by the people]
the life-giving ear of Demeter rises.
More frequently Δημήτριος καρπός [Demetrian fruit] is said, in manuscripts often written Δημήτρειος [Demetreios]: on which see Thes. vol. 2 p. 1071.
pasture of sheep and Demetrian livelihood.
the cattle before, the publicly abundant ones,
τὸ δήμιον [the public thing] the state, the government.
δαμαίων [of the public] (with a super w) and 879 δαμίαν [public] corruptly for δαναιᾶν [of the long-lived]. See δηναιός.
In both places I restored the Doric form δάμιον [public], preserved in M Ch. 56.
and you care for the public sacrifices.
for the city to have one public wound.
passing through the ears and the public mind.
and there are many public houses.
you are the city, you are the public thing.
the public thing, which rules the city.
with public clamor, spread by public rumor
joined with the clamor of the people, tossed about by the mouth and speech of the people.
where the remaining Doric forms δαμοθρόους [with public clamor] demand.

An adjective not read in other authors, except that Tzetzes Exeg. 11. p. 62, 22 called δημόθρουν κανόν [public rule] a trivial rule. The same is to be said about the three following adjectives δημόκραντος [ratified by the people] (from the verb κραίνειν [to accomplish]) δημόπρακτος [done by the people] δημορριφής [cast out by the people], which also are read only in Aeschylus.
yet public rumor has great strength.
you offered this sacrifice and public curses.
to accomplish) done by the people, cast out by the people
he pays the debt of a curse ratified by the people.
such a vote, done by the people, has been decided by the city.
thrown or cast out by the people.
cast out by the people – curses of stoning.
and may he not escape the fate of stoning by the people.
yet the people, having escaped evils, are harsh.
and the whole people of the Bactrians perishes.
I would not do these things without the people.
and the people would be more kindly to you.
the people have decreed full measures.
the ruling hand of the people, wherever it prevails.
where Meineke conjectured Ἀσιηνάν [Asian] or Ἀσιανάν [Asian]. More probably you would conjecture θήν [indeed], as I said in Thes. vol. 4 p. 364.
and they no longer are ruled by Persians throughout the land of Asia for long.

restored by L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 2 p. 885. In M in the former place τιμῶν δαμαίων [honors of the public] with a. over ῶν and a. over wv written by a corrector, in the latter place τιμᾶν δαμίαν [to honor the public].
